items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: Solid, secondary, outline, ghost, link and destructive buttons with a loading state and asChild for links.
items.docs: Use asChild to render the styles on a Next Link. loading disables the button and shows a spinner.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: Status and metadata labels with success, warning, destructive, outline and muted tones.
items.docs: Status badges carry text as well as colour; never rely on the tone alone.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.description: A loading placeholder in the shape of the content, with a shimmer sweep instead of a pulse. Give siblings a delay so the sweep runs as one wave.
items.docs: Match the real layout: a skeleton that does not hold the final shape shifts the page when the data arrives.

items.name: separator
items.title: Separator
items.description: A hairline rule, horizontal or vertical, decorative by default.

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: A keyboard key for shortcut hints, with a group for combinations.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: A text input with focus ring, invalid state and file input styling.
items.docs: Pair with Label via htmlFor. Set aria-invalid from your form library to show the error state. fieldSurface is the same surface for Textarea and the Select and Combobox triggers.

items.name: label
items.title: Label
items.description: A form label that focuses its control on click.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.description: A tooltip on hover and focus, with a shared provider so a row of controls feels like one surface.
items.docs: Wrap your app once in TooltipProvider. A tooltip is never the only place a label lives.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: A modal dialog with focus trap, Escape and backdrop close, and a required title and description.
items.docs: Every DialogContent needs a DialogTitle; hide it visually with sr-only if the design has no heading.

items.name: sheet
items.title: Sheet
items.description: A panel that slides in from any edge: menus, carts, filters. Same accessibility contract as Dialog.
items.docs: Pass side left, right, top or bottom. Sheets slide on transform only.

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: Tabs with arrow-key navigation, as an underline (line) or a segmented control (pill).
items.docs: Give TabsList the group/list class so the triggers pick up the variant.

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.description: A filtered, keyboard-driven list on cmdk, inline or as a palette in CommandDialog.
items.docs: CommandDialog brings its own Command root: put CommandInput and CommandList straight inside. It carries a hidden title and description for screen readers.

items.name: rhs-ui-theme
items.title: RHS UI theme
items.description: The RHS UI colour theme: a violet brand ramp on a constant OKLCH hue and a violet-tinted neutral scale, measured for WCAG AA in light and dark. Drops into any shadcn project as the semantic tokens.
items.docs: Installs the RHS semantic tokens into your globals.css. Your components keep their names (bg-background, text-primary); only the values change.

items.title: Select

items.name: select-demo
items.title: select demo
items.description: Interactive preview of the select component.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: A field that opens a searchable list, for choices too long to scan: countries, time zones, customers.

items.name: combobox-demo
items.title: combobox demo

items.name: textarea

items.name: textarea-demo
items.title: textarea demo

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover

items.name: popover-demo

items.name: dropdown-menu

items.name: navigation-menu

items.name: navigation-menu-demo

items.name: alert

items.name: alert-dialog-demo

items.docs: Give the group an aria-label. variant and size reach every button in it (Button, Copy, Async, Download, Upload and the rest) unless that button sets its own. items.name: split-button
items.title: Split button
items.description: A main action with a chevron that opens the alternatives, like Save and Save as draft: one click does the common thing, the menu holds the rest, and it can remember the choice.
items.docs: The chevron is named "More options for <label>". Loading and disabled apply to the main button only; a loading button is aria-disabled, not disabled, so keyboard focus stays on it. With remember, store the id from onRememberChange and pass it back as rememberedId on the next visit.

items.name: icon-button
items.title: Icon button
items.description: A button that is only an icon but can never be unlabelled: the label is required, shows as a tooltip with its shortcut, and the touch target stays 44px.
items.docs: label is required: it is the accessible name and the tooltip. shortcut only displays keys in the tooltip; bind the key with Shortcut button or your own handler. The badge can appear and disappear while the button has focus, and its count joins the accessible name. Wrap a toolbar in IconButtonProvider so the tooltips share one delay: after the first, the neighbours open at once. tooltip takes over the tooltip's open state.

items.name: async-button
items.title: Async button

items.name: download-button

items.docs: Give href for a file that exists (a real link; a cross-origin file may be opened instead of saved) or onDownload for one built when asked. Pass bytes as soon as you know the size; it can arrive after the first render. The accessible name follows the state and always holds the words drawn on the button.

items.name: upload-button
items.title: Upload button
items.description: A button that opens the file chooser, also takes drops and pastes, and hands you validated files, with progress on the button itself and a cancel while it uploads.
items.docs: You run the upload: pass state and progress back in. onFiles gets the accepted files and the rejected ones, each with a code and a reason in words (labels.accept replaces the words for what is accepted); show those wherever suits you, or hand the list to File Dropzone.

items.name: print-button
items.title: Print button

items.docs: Pass target as a ref or a selector. Mark anything that must stay off the paper with data-print-hide. The print styles are injected for the length of the job and removed on afterprint.

items.name: back-button
items.title: Back button
items.description: A back link that returns to where the person came from and falls back to a safe page when there is no history, so it never leaves your site.
items.docs: It is a real link to fallbackHref. Pass onBack to hand the press to your router: it gets true when the previous page is on your site and false when it is not.

items.name: back-button-demo

items.name: fullscreen-button
items.title: Fullscreen button
items.description: A toggle for fullscreen on any element: icon and label follow the real state, Escape works as the browser makes it, and it hides where unsupported.
items.docs: Mark the element with data-fullscreen-root or pass target, and keep the button inside it. iPhone Safari cannot expand an element: pass fallback to cover the viewport instead, or the button renders nothing there. With words on it the name is the visible label; the icon-only button keeps one name and uses aria-pressed.

items.name: shortcut-button
items.title: Shortcut button
items.description: A button that shows its keyboard shortcut and listens for it: the right modifier per platform, ignored while typing, exposed to assistive tech.
items.docs: mod is Cmd on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere. Sequences like "g i" time out after a second. The shortcut is ignored in text fields unless allowInInputs is set.

items.name: shortcut-button-demo

items.name: undo-redo-buttons
items.title: Undo and redo buttons
items.description: The undo and redo pair of any editor: dimmed when there is nothing to step through, the next step named in the tooltip, and the shortcuts bound for you.
items.docs: You own the history: keep it in a reducer or your editor and wire onUndo and onRedo. Pass the next step as undoLabel ("Undo: Move layer"); it becomes the tooltip and what a screen reader hears afterwards. The keys are ignored inside fields; pass scope to listen only inside an editor.

items.name: zoom-controls
items.title: Zoom controls
items.description: Zoom out, the current level, zoom in and fit: one compact control for images, maps, documents and canvases, with keyboard shortcuts and limits.
items.docs: value is a scale (1 is 100 percent); presets are in percent. The keys work while focus is inside the parent of the controls, or inside scope, so the browser's own zoom keeps working elsewhere. onFit adds Fit to screen: you know the content size, so you work out the scale.

items.name: record-navigator
items.title: Record navigator
items.description: Previous and next through a queue of records, with the position in words, keyboard shortcuts and the reason a button is off at either end.
items.docs: index counts from zero. Leave total out while a list is loading and the text reads "3 of many". With loop the buttons stay on at the ends and you wrap the index yourself. J and K are ignored while typing. For pages of rows use Pagination.

items.name: floating-action-button
items.title: Floating action button
items.description: The round primary action pinned to a corner: it extends to show its label, shrinks to the icon on scroll, and clears the bottom bar and safe area.
items.docs: It is fixed to the viewport; pass className="absolute" to pin it inside a positioned container. Give scrollTarget the ref of the element that scrolls when the page does not. offset lifts it over a bottom navigation, and visible hides it while a dialog is open. With href, disabled dims the link, takes it out of the tab order and stops the navigation.

items.name: speed-dial
items.title: Speed dial
items.description: A floating action that fans out three to five related actions on press, each labelled, reachable by keyboard and closing on Escape or an outside tap.
items.docs: The first action is the one nearest the trigger. Arrow keys move, Home and End jump, typing a letter finds an action, Escape closes. Like the floating action button it is fixed to the viewport; pass className="absolute" to keep it inside a container. direction="left" hangs each label above its button, so it needs short labels, and three actions take about 260px of width: on a phone use two or three.

items.name: speed-dial-demo

items.name: overflow-actions
items.title: Overflow actions
items.description: A row of actions that moves whatever does not fit into a More menu, by priority, measured on resize, so a toolbar works at every width.
items.docs: Give it the width of its container (it is a block, w-full). pinned actions never move; a lower priority leaves first. Use separatorBefore to keep groups in the menu, and onOverflowChange to learn which ids moved.

items.name: overflow-actions-demo
items.title: Overflow actions demo
items.description: A working preview of Overflow actions.

items.name: hold-to-confirm-button
items.title: Hold to confirm button
items.description: A destructive action you have to hold to trigger: a fill runs across the button, releasing early cancels, and a keyboard and screen reader path exists.
items.docs: onConfirm runs once. A quick press is the other way in: it says "Press again to confirm" and a second press within three seconds confirms. Keep label honest about the gesture ("Hold to delete project"); the button is as wide as its longest state.

items.name: hold-to-confirm-button-demo
items.title: Hold to confirm button demo
items.description: A working preview of Hold to confirm button.

items.name: resend-button
items.title: Resend button
items.description: A Resend code button with a cooldown: a live countdown while waiting, sending and sent states, and an attempt limit that says what to do next.
items.docs: onResend returns a promise; a rejection shows its message and does not start the timer. maxAttempts counts resends made with this button, and startCooling begins in the waiting state right after the first send. The countdown is announced only at the start, at 10 seconds and at 0, and the button's name stays "Resend code" (labels.ready) while it waits, so a screen reader is not told the time every second.

items.name: resend-button-demo
items.title: Resend button demo
items.description: A working preview of Resend button.

items.name: heading-anchor-link
items.title: Heading anchor link
items.description: The # beside a heading that lets a section be linked to: it copies the URL with the fragment, says so, and works from the keyboard.
items.docs: The id goes on the heading; without one no link is drawn. offset is the height of a sticky header, as scroll-margin-top. The link is a sibling of the heading, so the heading's own name stays clean for screen readers, and it is named after its heading (label takes {heading}), so a list of links tells them apart.

items.name: paste-button
items.title: Paste button
items.description: Paste from the clipboard with one press: it asks permission, checks the text, and says what it pasted, why it refused, or how to allow access.
items.docs: The clipboard is read only when the button is pressed. Pass targetRef to fill and focus an input, and validate to refuse text with a reason. Where the browser blocks or lacks readText it focuses the field and says to press Ctrl V; pass read for a native shell.

items.name: paste-button-demo

items.name: autoplay-toggle
items.title: Autoplay toggle
items.description: The pause control moving content must have: one button to stop and start a carousel, ticker or video, with a hook that also holds it on hover, focus and hidden tabs.
items.docs: label says what it controls and is part of the name (Pause testimonials, Play testimonials). Let useAutoplay own the state, spread contentProps on the moving content and read running in the timer; there is no aria-pressed because the name already follows the state.

items.name: insert-between-button
items.title: Insert between button
items.description: The plus that appears between two items so you can insert one right there: on hover and focus, always on touch, and reachable by keyboard.
items.docs: index is the position the new item takes; the name reads Insert step between 2 and 3 (pass between for real names). Put one in every gap of your list, and move focus to the new item in onInsert.

items.name: swap-button
items.title: Swap button
items.description: Swap two values with one press, like origin and destination or from and to: the icon turns, both fields trade places, and it says what changed.
items.docs: Give it labelA, labelB and the current values so it can say what changed. With seam it centres on its parent, which must be relative, and reaches (size minus gap) / 2 into each field: leave a 20px gap between fields padded 16px (gap-5) so it clears their text and its focus ring has room. swapValues(state, 'from', 'to') is a pure helper for the common two-field state.

items.description: A badge for a record's state with a glyph and a word, so draft, paid, overdue and archived read without colour.
items.docs: Pass any string as status; known keys get their glyph and emphasis, others get a neutral outline. Extend the vocabulary with statuses, spreading defaultStatuses. The text is the status; the dot size keeps an sr-only label.

items.name: chip
items.title: Chip
items.description: A compact pill that is static, selectable or removable, with an icon or avatar: the unit behind filters, picks and attributes.
items.docs: toggle chips are buttons with aria-pressed and a check. An input chip's remove button is named Remove <label>; Backspace or Delete on it removes the chip and focus moves to its neighbour. Pass removeLabel when the label is not plain text.

items.title: Chip demo

items.name: tag-list
items.title: Tag list
items.description: A row of tags that never breaks the layout: it shows what fits, then a '+3' button that opens the rest.
items.docs: Give the list a width to fit into (a table column or max-w class), then fit shows what fits and max caps the count; before it has measured, the server HTML shows only the whole tags that fit one line. The group is named like Design, Research and 3 more. Tags with an href are links; others call onTagSelect.

items.name: tag-list-demo
items.title: Tag list demo
items.description: A working preview of Tag list.

items.name: formatted-number
items.title: Formatted number
items.description: Numbers formatted for the reader: compact (1.2K), percent, unit or currency, in tabular figures with the full value kept for assistive technology.
items.docs: The Intl style option is called format here, because style belongs to CSS. percent takes a fraction (0.12 is 12%); currency needs currency and unit needs unit, which the types enforce, and if Intl still refuses a code it writes a plain decimal with the code. Compact figures keep the full number in the accessible name and a tooltip that opens on hover and on a tap; add focusable for a keyboard tab stop. null and NaN show the placeholder.

items.name: formatted-number-demo
items.title: Formatted number demo
items.description: A working preview of Formatted number.

items.name: money-amount
items.title: Money amount
items.description: An amount of money with currency, sign and meaning in words, for credits, debits and refunds, in tabular figures.
items.docs: amount is an integer in minor units (1250 is 12.50; JPY has none); a fraction is rounded to the nearest minor unit. direction credit, debit, refund or auto (the sign of the amount) decides the sign, the weight and the sr-only word. A currency code Intl rejects is written as digits and the code. Meaning never depends on red and green.

items.name: money-amount-demo
items.title: Money amount demo
items.description: A working preview of Money amount.

items.name: link-card
items.title: Link card
items.description: A card that is one link: icon or image, title, description and an arrow, with a focus ring around the whole card.
items.docs: The title is the only link, stretched over the card. With asChild, pass your framework link as the child (a Next Link with no text and its own href); the title is added inside it. external adds an arrow and a hidden opens in a new tab.

items.name: link-card-demo
items.title: Link card demo

items.name: due-date-label
items.title: Due date label
items.description: A due date in words that matter: 'Due today', 'Due in 3 days' or 'Overdue by 2 days', with an icon that carries the urgency.
items.docs: Days are compared as calendar days in timeZone, so a task due today never reads overdue at 00:01. A date-only string like 2026-10-24 is a calendar date and never shifts. The full date is in a tooltip that opens on hover and on a tap; add focusable for a keyboard tab stop, or showDate to write it into the line (Due in 3 days · Fri 23 Oct) for phones and print. Pass now for tests; otherwise it reads the browser clock after hydration.

items.title: Due date label demo
items.description: A working preview of Due date label.

items.name: inline-code
items.title: Inline code
items.description: Code inside a sentence: a quiet mono chip that wraps cleanly, with an optional click to copy.
items.docs: It inherits the surrounding font size. copyable turns the chip into a Copy button; pass value when the children are not plain text. Your other props land on the code, or on the button when it is copyable. Plain inline code is a Server Component; only the copyable part is a client module.

items.title: Inline code demo
items.description: A working preview of Inline code.

items.name: copyable-text
items.title: Copyable text
items.description: A value you copy with one click, such as an order id, an email or a hash: the text is the button, the icon is always visible, and a check confirms the copy in place.
items.docs: label names what is copied, so the button reads "Copy order id: ORD-1048". display writes a short form while value is copied whole, and truncate="middle" keeps the end of a long id visible. A value that wraps carries its icon along, so it stays beside the last word. Where the browser blocks the clipboard the text is selected and the tooltip asks for Ctrl C. status shows the copied or the blocked state without a press, for a preview.

items.name: copyable-text-demo
items.title: Copyable text demo
items.description: A working preview of Copyable text.

items.name: middle-truncate
items.title: Middle truncate
items.description: Truncates in the middle so file names, hashes and URLs keep their ending, in pure CSS: quarterly-report-fin…2026.pdf, with the whole text for screen readers and the tooltip.
items.docs: Two spans, a start that truncates and an end that never shrinks, so there is no measuring. tail sets how many end characters stay; left out, a file keeps its extension and about five characters before it, moved to the start of the nearest word, so the end reads harbour.jpg and not rbour.jpg. In a table cell, give the table a fixed layout or the cell a max width, and in a flex row give the text min-w-0.

items.name: middle-truncate-demo
items.title: Middle truncate demo
items.description: A working preview of Middle truncate.

items.name: match-highlight
items.title: Match highlight
items.description: Marks the part of a string that matches a search with a real mark element, ignoring case and accents, with several terms and no regular expression to break.
items.docs: The query is matched as plain text, so typing a bracket never throws. "cafe" marks Café and cafetière; caseSensitive and accentSensitive turn either off. Pass an array of terms to mark each of them, and markClassName to restyle the mark.

items.name: match-highlight-demo
items.title: Match highlight demo
items.description: A working preview of Match highlight.

items.name: check-list
items.title: Check list
items.description: A list with a check or a dash on each line: what is included and what is not, said in words for screen readers, with hints and tooltips for plan cards and requirements.
items.docs: Every line carries a hidden "Included" or "Not included". tone="inverted" is for a card with a solid fill: the focus ring and the tooltip swap colours there, so both still show on the card. A line with a tooltip gets a small info button that opens on hover, focus and tap; without tooltips the list is a Server Component.

items.name: check-list-demo
items.title: Check list demo
items.description: A working preview of Check list.

items.name: step-list
items.title: Step list
items.description: How-to steps for docs: numbered markers on a hairline that ends after the last step, a real ordered list, and any content (text, code, images) inside each step.
items.docs: Numbers come from a CSS counter, so any content between steps keeps its place. start continues a guide, summaryOnly folds every step to its title for an overview, and a step with an id can be linked to. Pick the heading level of the titles with as.

items.name: step-list-demo
items.title: Step list demo
items.description: A working preview of Step list.

items.name: date-tile
items.title: Date tile
items.description: The little calendar leaf: month, day and weekday in a small fixed-width square for event lists, deadlines and invoices, with today, past and range variants.
items.docs: A time element with the calendar day in dateTime; a screen reader hears the whole date. tone="today" inverts the tile and adds "Today" to what is heard; you decide what is today, so the server and the browser never disagree. A date-only string never shifts with the time zone.

items.name: date-tile-demo
items.title: Date tile demo
items.description: A working preview of Date tile.

items.name: date-range-text
items.title: Date range text
items.description: A date range written the way people say it: 12 to 15 March 2026, with the shared month and year said once, times, open ends and nights, in the reader's language.
items.docs: Built on Intl.DateTimeFormat formatRangeToParts, with a time element for each end. English reads "to"; other languages keep their own range mark, or pass separator. includeTime adds the clock, nights appends "3 nights", and a missing start or end reads "from" or "until". Pass labels for those words in another language.

items.name: date-range-text-demo
items.title: Date range text demo
items.description: A working preview of Date range text.

items.name: duration-text
items.title: Duration text
items.description: A duration in few characters that still reads in full aloud: 1h 30m for the eye, 1 hour, 30 minutes for the ear, with an ISO 8601 value for machines.
items.docs: Built on the Intl number and list formats, not the newer duration format, so the server and the browser write the same text. format is narrow, short, long or clock; largestUnit and maxUnits decide how much is written, and the rest is cut, not rounded. Zero reads 0m.

items.name: duration-text-demo
items.title: Duration text demo
items.description: A working preview of Duration text.

items.name: masked-value
items.title: Masked value
items.description: A sensitive value hidden until asked, such as •••• 4242 or j•••@example.com, with a reveal button that says what it does and a timer that hides it again.
items.docs: While hidden the markup holds only the masked text. The value is still a prop, so from a Server Component it is in the page payload: fetch it in onReveal if that matters. mask is card, email, phone, iban, full or your own function (from a client component); autoHideAfter hides it again and a polite status says so. Control it with revealed and onRevealedChange.

items.name: masked-value-demo
items.title: Masked value demo
items.description: A working preview of Masked value.

items.name: show-more-list
items.title: Show more list
items.description: A list that shows its first few items and a Show 7 more reviews button for the rest, with focus kept on the button and the count announced politely.
items.docs: Pass items and renderItem, or the drawn items as children when you are in a Server Component, where a function cannot be passed. noun names what the button reveals, as a string or as { one, other } when a single item can be left; step reveals in chunks. It works on data already in memory and makes no request. New items ease in unless reduced motion is on.

items.name: show-more-list-demo
items.title: Show more list demo
items.description: A working preview of Show more list.

items.name: country-label
items.title: Country label
items.description: A country, language or currency named in the reader's language from a code, with its flag tile: for tables, addresses and profiles, with no data file.
items.docs: Names come from Intl.DisplayNames. The flag is built from regional indicator letters in a tile of fixed size, so a platform without flag glyphs shows the two letters and the layout does not move. Chrome and Edge on Windows are such a platform: add a flag polyfill font such as Twemoji Country Flags to the font stack of your page to show flags there. Languages and currencies get a tile with their code or symbol; an unknown code shows itself, or your fallback.

items.name: country-label-demo
items.title: Country label demo
items.description: A working preview of Country label.

items.name: code-tabs
items.title: Code tabs
items.description: The same code in several languages or package managers as tabs that remember your choice across the page, with copy, a stable height and an optional localStorage key.
items.docs: Wrap the pages that show code in a CodeTabsProvider once, in a layout, and every CodeTabs with the same group switches together. storageKey keeps the choice in localStorage; it is read after the page has loaded, so the server and the first paint show defaultTab. All panels share one cell, so the block is as high as the tallest.

items.name: code-tabs-demo
items.title: Code tabs demo
items.description: A working preview of Code tabs.

items.name: review-score
items.title: Review score
items.description: A review score in a box with a word: 8.9 Excellent and the review count, the compact rating for listings, named in full for screen readers.
items.docs: The whole is named "Rated 8.9 out of 10, Excellent, 1,204 reviews". The word comes from bands you can set with labels, and the fill of the box (solid, outlined, quiet) repeats it, so strength never depends on colour. A score without reviews says "No reviews yet". href makes it a link.

items.name: review-score-demo
items.title: Review score demo
items.description: A working preview of Review score.

items.name: barcode
items.title: Barcode
items.description: Scannable Code 128 and EAN-13 barcodes as SVG for tickets, labels and packing slips, with the check digit handled and the value in text below.
items.docs: Code 128 takes any ASCII text and chooses its own code sets; EAN-13 takes twelve digits (the check digit is added) or thirteen (it is checked), and a value that cannot be encoded is reported in words instead of drawn. The quiet zone and black on white are fixed because a scanner needs them. encodeBarcode and eanCheckDigit are exported for validating a value before you print it.

items.name: barcode-demo
items.title: Barcode demo
items.description: A working preview of Barcode.

items.name: loading-overlay
items.title: Loading overlay
items.description: Covers a card, table or form while it refreshes with a scrim, a spinner and a label, and makes the stale content inert so it cannot be clicked or tabbed into.
items.docs: Wrap the region and set loading. delay (default 200 ms) keeps a quick refresh from flashing the overlay, and minDuration (default 400 ms) keeps it from blinking once it is up. Give the component the radius of the region it covers, for example className="rounded-xl". The content is made inert and aria-busy while the overlay shows; focus that was inside it is parked on the overlay and handed back.

items.name: loading-overlay-demo
items.title: Loading overlay demo
items.description: A working preview of Loading overlay.

items.name: skeleton-group
items.title: Skeleton group
items.description: Wraps skeleton placeholders so they read as one Loading to screen readers and sweep as one wave, with no delays wired by hand.
items.docs: Put Skeleton blocks inside, at any depth: the group staggers their shimmer in document order, marks the region aria-busy and renders one visually hidden status instead of a dozen silent boxes. When loading turns false the placeholders are not rendered and nothing is announced. A custom shape joins the wave with data-skeleton, or asks for a delay with useSkeletonDelay(index).

items.name: skeleton-group-demo
items.title: Skeleton group demo
items.description: A working preview of Skeleton group.

items.name: text-skeleton
items.title: Text skeleton
items.description: Lines of loading text with natural, uneven lengths and a short last line, each bar in the line height of the text it stands in for.
items.docs: Pick the size of the text it replaces (sm, base, lg or a heading level h1 to h6) and the number of lines: every bar sits in one line box of that text, so the real content moves nothing when it arrives. Line lengths come from a seed, so the block is identical on the server and in the browser; give neighbouring blocks different seeds. Wrap a screen in SkeletonGroup to announce Loading once.

items.name: text-skeleton-demo
items.title: Text skeleton demo
items.description: A working preview of Text skeleton.

items.name: async-view
items.title: Async view
items.description: Every state of a data view in one wrapper: loading, error with Retry, empty, background refresh and ready, each with a slot and a default.
items.docs: It fetches nothing: pass status ('loading' | 'error' | 'empty' | 'ready') and isFetching from TanStack Query, SWR or a plain useState. The skeleton waits loadingDelay (200 ms) so a quick load never flashes one; a background refresh keeps the old content and runs a thin bar along the top. The region carries aria-busy and a polite status announces each change. Pass skeleton, error and empty to replace a default, or errorTitle, errorMessage and onRetry to adjust the built-in error panel.

items.name: async-view-demo
items.title: Async view demo
items.description: A working preview of Async view.

items.name: error-boundary
items.title: Error boundary
items.description: A React error boundary with a calm built-in fallback, a reset that really remounts the subtree, resetKeys, and a hook for your error logger.
items.docs: Wrap any subtree: when a child throws while rendering, the fallback replaces it and the rest of the page keeps working. fallback is a node or a function that gets { error, reset } (a function needs a Client Component parent); onError is the place for your logger; resetKeys resets the boundary when a route, an id or a filter changes; reset mounts the children anew. withErrorBoundary lives in error-boundary/with-error-boundary and is not a client module. Event handlers, async code and the server are outside what a boundary catches: use error.tsx for the page.

items.name: error-boundary-demo
items.title: Error boundary demo
items.description: A working preview of Error boundary.

items.name: live-announcer
items.title: Live announcer
items.description: One place to tell screen readers what just happened: mount LiveAnnouncer once, then announce polite or urgent messages from any component with a hook.
items.docs: Mount <LiveAnnouncer /> once, as a sibling of your app's main wrapper rather than inside it, so a modal that hides the app does not hide it. Then call announce('3 results found') or announce('Upload failed', 'assertive'), or take the same function from useAnnounce(). Both regions exist from the first render, a message is written by emptying and refilling its region so repeats are read again, identical messages sent within 600 ms count as one, and the rest are read in turn. clearAfterMs empties a region after a message; onAnnounce reports each message that was written, for a visible log. A no-op on the server.

items.name: live-announcer-demo
items.title: Live announcer demo
items.description: A working preview of Live announcer.

items.name: undo-toast
items.title: Undo toast
items.description: The delete-with-undo pattern: the row goes at once, a toast offers Undo with a draining timer, and the real delete runs only when the time is up.
items.docs: Call toastUndo({ message, onUndo, onCommit }) from the handler that removes the row, after you have removed it from your own state. onUndo puts it back; onCommit runs once, when the six seconds are up, when the toast is closed or pushed out by a newer one, and when the page is left (make the request with keepalive or sendBeacon there). The line drains over duration and waits while the toast is hovered or has focus and while the tab is in the background. Mount Toaster once, as for any toast.

items.name: undo-toast-demo
items.title: Undo toast demo
items.description: A working preview of Undo toast.

items.name: task-toast
items.title: Task toast
items.description: One toast that follows a task from start to finish: a spinner, a live progress bar, then success, or a failure with Retry, all in the same toast.
items.docs: const task = taskToast({ title: 'Exporting orders', onCancel }); then task.progress(0.4, '1,200 of 3,000 orders'), task.success('Export ready', { action }) or task.error('Export failed', { onRetry }). It is one toast the whole way and changes in place: a spinner, a slim bar with a percentage, a check that closes itself after five seconds, or a warning that stays until it is dealt with. If someone closes the toast by hand while the task runs, the result still arrives as a toast; task.dismiss() closes it for good. taskToast.promise(promise, { loading, success, error }) covers a task with no progress to report. Mount Toaster once, as for any toast. The Toaster shows the last three toasts, so a fourth can push out an error toast together with its Retry: for a long job, keep Retry reachable elsewhere as well.

items.name: task-toast-demo
items.title: Task toast demo
items.description: A working preview of Task toast.

items.name: dismissible-notice
items.title: Dismissible notice
items.description: A tip or notice card people can close for good: it remembers the dismissal, can return after N days, and comes back when its version changes.
items.docs: id names the notice in localStorage (rhs-ui:dismissed:<id>); version and remindAfterDays decide when a dismissal stops counting. Where storage throws, the dismissal lives in memory for the session. The card is drawn after the page is live, never in the server HTML, and it folds away on close, instantly under reduced motion. useDismissed(id, options) returns { dismissed, dismiss, restore } for anything else that should stay closed: pass dismiss to Banner's onDismiss and render the banner while dismissed is false.

items.name: dismissible-notice-demo
items.title: Dismissible notice demo
items.description: A working preview of Dismissible notice.

items.name: last-updated
items.title: Last updated
items.description: An Updated 3 min ago label with a refresh button that keeps itself current, and says in words and weight when the data has gone stale.
items.docs: updatedAt takes a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string. The text counts minutes, then gives a clock time after an hour (with the date once it is not today), written in locale and timeZone so the server and the browser agree; before the page is live it shows the date and time instead of an age. Past staleAfterMs (15 minutes) it adds a warning mark and 'may be out of date'. onRefresh shows the button: return a promise and the arrow turns until it settles (a rejection stops it without saying Data refreshed), or drive refreshing yourself. labels takes your own words as templates with {n}, {time}, {date} and {text}.

items.name: last-updated-demo
items.title: Last updated demo
items.description: A working preview of Last updated.

items.name: new-items-pill
items.title: New items pill
items.description: The floating pill over a live feed or chat that counts what arrived, scrolls to it on click and hides itself once the reader gets there.
items.docs: Put it inside a relative wrapper next to the scroller and pass scrollRef (give the scroller tabIndex 0 so it can be scrolled by keyboard); without scrollRef the page itself is watched and the pill wants a fixed position. count is how many items arrived while the reader was away. onClick runs before the scroll, so merge your buffered items there; onReach runs when the reader gets to the new content on their own, so you can merge and reset the count. label takes a string with {count}, or one, other and so on for plural forms.

items.name: new-items-pill-demo
items.title: New items pill demo
items.description: A working preview of New items pill.

items.name: infinite-scroll-status
items.title: Infinite scroll status
items.description: The footer of an auto-loading list: it asks for the next page near the viewport, then shows loading, an error with Retry, or the end.
items.docs: Place it after the last item. Set loading while a page is being fetched: that is what lets it ask again when the new page still leaves it in view. When the list scrolls inside a box, pass that box as root so rootMargin applies to it. A Load more button stays visible as the fallback for keyboard users and browsers without IntersectionObserver; pressing it, or Retry, keeps keyboard focus in the footer while the page comes. Pass count (and total) to have what each page added announced.

items.name: infinite-scroll-status-demo
items.title: Infinite scroll status demo
items.description: A working preview of Infinite scroll status.

items.name: pull-to-refresh
items.title: Pull to refresh
items.description: The mobile pull-down gesture for refreshing a list: an elastic indicator, a spinner while it works, and a visible Refresh button for everyone else.
items.docs: Give the component a height: the list scrolls inside it, is reachable by keyboard, and listLabel names it. onRefresh returns the promise of the work; the spinner stays until it settles. Only touch input starts a pull, so wheels and desktop scrolling are untouched, and the Refresh button in the bar runs the same handler. The scroller sets overscroll-behavior so the browser's own refresh does not fight it. Letting go early, or taking the finger back above where it began, cancels the pull.

items.name: pull-to-refresh-demo
items.title: Pull to refresh demo
items.description: A working preview of Pull to refresh.

items.name: eta-progress
items.title: ETA progress
items.description: A progress bar that says how long is left, from the real pace so far, with an estimate that is smoothed so the text stays calm.
items.docs: Pass value (0 to 1) and startedAt. The text says Calculating for the first seconds, then an estimate rounded to friendly steps that only changes when it has drifted meaningfully, then Almost done and Finished in 1 min 20 s. The bar's aria-valuetext holds the sentence, and the sentence is announced at most every 15 seconds. Pass finishedAt when you know when it ended; now freezes the clock for tests and snapshots.

items.name: eta-progress-demo
items.title: ETA progress demo
items.description: A working preview of ETA progress.

items.name: strength-meter
items.title: Strength meter
items.description: A four-segment strength bar with a word for the level and the one thing to fix next, for passwords and other scored input.
items.docs: Hand it the 0 to 4 score of whichever estimator you use (zxcvbn's fits as it is) and an optional hint. Point your field's aria-describedby at the id. labels takes the five words for another language. A change is announced politely once it has held still for 800 ms. It stands alone from a password rules checklist, and the two can sit together.

items.name: strength-meter-demo
items.title: Strength meter demo
items.description: A working preview of Strength meter.

items.name: milestone-progress
items.title: Milestone progress
items.description: A progress bar with named stops along the way, for goals with steps: a funding target, a loyalty ladder, free-shipping tiers.
items.docs: Pass value, max and milestones ({ at, label }). formatValue turns a number into words ("1,280 points") for the value, the stops and the next-stop line. nextLabel is the template for that line, with {remaining} and {milestone}; the last stop reads Goal reached. Reached stops carry a check, upcoming ones a ring, and the list says so in words. On a narrow container the labels alternate above and below the track.

items.name: milestone-progress-demo
items.title: Milestone progress demo
items.description: A working preview of Milestone progress.

items.name: estimated-progress
items.title: Estimated progress
items.description: A bar for work with no progress signal: it eases toward 90 percent on an expected duration and only finishes when the work does.
items.docs: Give it expectedMs and a status (running, done or failed). The fill follows an ease-out curve toward 90 percent and never reaches it by itself; done fills the rest, failed freezes it in the destructive tone. It says About 30 seconds at first and Still working once the expected time has passed. Pass startedAt when the work began before the component mounted. Under reduced motion the fill moves in 10 percent steps.

items.name: estimated-progress-demo
items.title: Estimated progress demo
items.description: A working preview of Estimated progress.

items.name: slow-loading-state
items.title: Slow loading state
items.description: A loader that gets more honest the longer it waits: quiet at first, then a reassuring line, then Cancel and Try again.
items.docs: Wrap the content that will appear when loading ends. Nothing shows for the first 300 ms (delay), then a spinner and the label; thresholds are two plain numbers in ms, 8000 and 20000 by default, for the reassuring line and for Cancel and Try again. Each stage is announced politely. Everything resets when loading flips or Try again is pressed. When Cancel or Try again goes away, keyboard focus rests on the component; move it on in onCancel to the content or the trigger.

items.name: slow-loading-state-demo
items.title: Slow loading state demo
items.description: A working preview of Slow loading state.

items.name: activity-toast
items.title: Activity toast
items.description: A toast for what someone else just did: their avatar, the action, a time and View, merging bursts into one counted toast.
items.docs: Mount the house Toaster once, then call toastActivity({ actor, action, target, at, group, onView }). Events with the same group inside mergeWindow merge into one toast whose count updates in place; mergedLabel is the sentence for that, with {count} and {target}, and moreLabel words the overflow after two names, with {count}. An actor with self: true is skipped, so it never shows for the person's own actions. The toast pauses on hover and focus like every toast and is announced politely once.

items.name: activity-toast-demo
items.title: Activity toast demo
items.description: A working preview of Activity toast.

items.name: optimistic-item
items.title: Optimistic item
items.description: Wraps a list item the server has not confirmed yet: dimmed and busy while pending, with Retry and Discard if it failed.
items.docs: Wrap a row, comment or card and pass status: confirmed adds nothing, pending dims the item and marks it busy without blocking it, failed keeps it visible with Could not save and Retry and Discard buttons. error says why. Moving from pending to confirmed is instant and silent; a failure is announced once as an alert and focus is never moved by it (after Retry it rests on the item). Keep the top right corner of the wrapped item free: the pending spinner sits there.

items.name: optimistic-item-demo
items.title: Optimistic item demo
items.description: A working preview of Optimistic item.

items.name: update-highlight
items.title: Update highlight
items.description: Marks a row, card or number that just changed with a tint that fades out, an "Updated" marker when motion is reduced and a polite message for screen readers.
items.docs: Hand it a changeKey: the value, a version or a timestamp. When the key changes, the element is tinted with the foreground colour and fades over duration (1500 ms). The first value is never marked unless skipFirst is false, and changes that land while it is fading restart the same highlight. Nothing is added inside the element, so asChild works on a table row (the tint is then drawn on its cells). Under reduced motion, or with reduceMotion, there is no fade: a small marker with label hangs on the top edge for a few seconds. Pass label or announce and a screen reader hears a polite message on every change; messages that arrive together are read as one.

items.name: update-highlight-demo
items.title: Update highlight demo
items.description: A working preview of Update highlight.

items.name: email-field
items.title: Email field
items.description: An email input that catches typos before they cost a signup: it offers the likely domain, such as gmail.com for gmial.com, and reports a clean address.
items.docs: Controlled with value and onValueChange(email, { valid }), or uncontrolled with defaultValue. The reported address is trimmed with its domain in lower case, and name sends that clean form in a hidden input. Nothing shows while typing: on leaving the field a malformed address is explained in words, or, when the domain is one or two edits from a provider in domains, a button offers 'Use rick@gmail.com instead'. Set suggest={false} to turn the suggestion off. The domain list, editDistance, suggestEmail, describeEmail and isValidEmail are exported from email-field/emails for your own checks. Set noValidate on the form if you prefer these messages to the browser's own.

items.title: Email field demo
items.description: A working preview of Email field.

items.name: username-field
items.title: Username field
items.description: A handle field with an @ prefix, the rules stated in words and an availability check you supply, so people know a name is free before they submit.
items.docs: Give it onCheck(username, { signal }) and it asks once typing has paused for debounce ms (400 by default): return true or false, or { available, suggestions } with up to three names that are free. Pass the signal to fetch so a question for an older name is cancelled; an answer for an older name is thrown away either way. onStatusChange(status, username) says when the name is available, for example to enable a submit button. reserved takes names that are refused without asking, and RESERVED_USERNAMES in username-field/usernames is a starting list. Without onCheck the field only checks the format and calls nothing.

items.name: username-field-demo
items.title: Username field demo
items.description: A working preview of Username field.

items.name: url-field
items.title: URL field
items.description: A web address field with a protocol menu: paste a full link and it splits, type a bare domain and it adds https, and it reports one clean URL.
items.docs: value is the whole address and onValueChange(url, { valid }) reports one clean URL: the protocol from the menu, the host in lower case and the rest as typed. A pasted link moves its protocol into the menu. protocols sets the menu (the first is used for a bare domain), requireHttps refuses http:// and offers a switch to https://, allowPath={false} takes a bare domain only, and name sends the URL in a hidden input. A valid address gets a link that opens a new tab with rel noopener noreferrer. The checks run when the field is left, then follow the typing until the address is right.

items.name: url-field-demo
items.title: URL field demo
items.description: A working preview of URL field.

items.name: slug-field
items.title: Slug field
items.description: A URL slug that writes itself from the title until you edit it, shows the final address and hands control back with a single click.
items.docs: Pass the title and the slug follows it. value and onValueChange(slug, { auto }) make it controlled; a slug that is there when the field mounts starts locked, because someone chose it, and so does one that arrives from outside later (the saved slug of a record that loads after the form), unless it is only the slug the field itself reported while following the title. Typing locks it, and the Follow title button or an emptied field gives it back. baseUrl feeds the preview, taken flags a clash and offers the next free slug, maxLength cuts it. slugify(text, maxLength), cleanSlugInput and nextFreeSlug are exported from slug-field/slugify. Letters of other scripts have no plain form and are dropped by slugify: transliterate them first.

items.name: slug-field-demo
items.title: Slug field demo
items.description: A working preview of Slug field.

items.name: name-field
items.title: Name field
items.description: A person's name without the usual mistakes: no forced first and last split, sensible casing on blur and Dutch and other name particles respected.
items.docs: One field for the whole name; onValueChange receives { full, given, particle, family }. On leaving the field, a name typed all in lower case or all in capitals gets its capitals, with the words in particles (lower case) kept down after the first word. Mixed case is never touched. The change is announced, and Undo restores exactly what was typed and stays undone for that text. splitable adds a Split into parts disclosure (defaultOpen starts it open), and with name the three parts also go out as name-given, name-particle and name-family. splitName, joinName and fixNameCase are exported from name-field/names.

items.name: name-field-demo
items.title: Name field demo
items.description: A working preview of Name field.

items.name: masked-input
items.title: Masked input
items.description: A text input that formats as you type from a simple pattern such as (###) ###-#### or AA-####, with a caret that never jumps.
items.docs: mask: # is a digit, A a letter (made a capital), * a letter or a digit, a backslash makes the next character a literal, and anything else is written for you. value and onValueChange(raw, formatted, { complete }) work with the bare characters. showMask draws the unfilled part as quiet text, and definitions adds tokens such as { H: /[0-9a-f]/i } or replaces #, A and *. inputMode is numeric when the mask only takes digits. The field is not controlled by React, because the caret has to be set by hand after every edit; name posts the formatted text.

items.name: masked-input-demo
items.title: Masked input demo
items.description: A working preview of Masked input.

items.name: date-field
items.title: Date field
items.description: A date you can type: day, month and year as separate segments in your locale's order, stepping with the arrow keys, with an optional calendar button.
items.docs: value and onValueChange(iso, { valid }) speak ISO dates (2026-03-14), with an empty string while the date is incomplete or impossible. The order of the parts and the separator come from locale (en-US by default), and min and max are ISO dates. Digits move on by themselves, ArrowUp and ArrowDown step a part, Backspace clears it and a pasted date fills all three (a two-digit year is 20xx up to 68, 19xx from 69). An impossible date such as 31 February is explained once all three parts are filled. showCalendar adds a button that opens the Calendar in a popover under the field, name adds a hidden input with the ISO date, and labels renames the parts for another language. id goes on the first part, so a label's htmlFor focuses the field; name the whole group with aria-labelledby.

items.name: time-field
items.title: Time field
items.description: A time you can type: hours and minutes as segments, in 24-hour or 12-hour form, stepping with the arrow keys and compact enough for a table cell.
items.docs: value and onValueChange speak 24-hour times ("14:30"), with null while the time is incomplete or outside min and max, the same shape as the Time picker, so the two can be swapped. The locale decides the clock, the order of the parts and the separator (en-US writes AM and PM, nl-NL writes 24 hours), and hour12 overrides it either way. Digits move on by themselves (a 7 can only be 07), ArrowUp and ArrowDown step a part and wrap round (the minutes in steps of minuteStep, 15 puts 07 on 15), Backspace clears it, typing a or p sets AM or PM and a tap on the period turns it over (a mouse click only focuses it the first time, and turns it over from the second click on). A part left with one digit is written out in full, so a 2 in the minutes is 02. A pasted time (14:30, 2:30 pm, 1430) fills every part. min and max are 24-hour times; a time outside them is explained with the range written the way the clock is (Pick a time between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM.), and min later than max is a range through midnight. size="sm" and showIcon={false} make it fit a table cell. name adds a hidden input with the 24-hour time, labels renames the parts for another language, and id goes on the first part, so a label's htmlFor focuses the field; name the group with aria-labelledby.

items.name: birthday-field
items.title: Birthday field
items.description: A date of birth without a calendar: day, month by name and a typed year, with the age rule checked in words and the right autofill tokens set.
items.docs: value and onValueChange(iso, { valid }) speak ISO dates (1990-03-14), with an empty string while the date is incomplete, impossible or not allowed; only the date is reported, never an age. The order of the three parts and the names of the months come from locale (en-US by default). minAge and maxAge are whole years, the age rules are checked from today in the reader's own time zone, and today (an ISO date) pins the clock for a server or a test. A date that does not exist (31 February), that is in the future or that breaks an age rule is explained in words, the wrong part is marked red, and the one message under the group is what the group's aria-describedby points at; with a valid date the same line tells a screen reader the date it understood. A day over 31 and a year of one to three digits left behind are noticed at once. messages replaces the words (tooYoung and tooOld are functions of the age), labels renames the small labels and placeholders for another language. The parts carry autocomplete bday-day, bday-month and bday-year; the month is the house select, whose hidden native select is what a browser fills, so keep the field inside a form for autofill. name adds a hidden input with the ISO date, and id goes on the first part, so a label's htmlFor focuses the field; name the group with aria-labelledby.

items.name: scoped-search-field
items.title: Scoped search field
items.description: A search box with a scope menu attached, for searching in Docs, People or Files, that reports the query and the scope together.
items.docs: scopes is a list of { value, label, placeholder, icon }: the first is chosen at the start, and scope with onScopeChange (or defaultScope) controls it. The empty field shows the placeholder of the chosen scope (Search people by name or email), so it always says what it will search. query, defaultQuery and onQueryChange work the same way for the text. Changing the scope keeps the text and announces Searching in People in a polite live region; choosing it from the open menu also moves the focus on to the field, ready to type. onSearch(query, scope) is called with the trimmed text when Enter is pressed, not for an empty field unless allowEmpty is set; inside a form the form still submits, and name and scopeName put the text and the scope in the submitted data. The first Escape clears the text and the second leaves the field. The field answers to its own width, not the screen's: below 20rem (a container query) the menu shrinks to the scope's icon (the first letter of its label in a small chip when a scope has none) and the shortcut hint goes, while the scope stays in the menu's accessible name (Search in People; scopeLabel changes the first words). The shortcut is a hint only: bind the key yourself. Other input props such as autoFocus and aria-label go to the input, whose accessible name is its placeholder unless you give one.

items.name: recent-searches-field
items.title: Recent searches field
items.description: A search field that remembers: focus it and your recent queries appear, each removable, with a clear all action and full keyboard use.
items.docs: recent is the list, newest first, and onRecentChange hands back the new list when a search runs (it moves to the top, and the same search from earlier is not kept twice), when one is removed and when all are cleared: the field stores nothing, so the history can live in state, local storage or on a server. onSearch(query) runs on Enter or when a recent search is chosen. While the field is focused and empty the list opens (max entries, 6 by default); once text is typed it narrows to the recent searches that begin with it, ignoring case and accents, with the typed part in bold, and when nothing matches the panel stays shut. The focus never leaves the input: the arrow keys move a highlight that is announced through aria-activedescendant, Enter runs the highlighted search or the text, Delete removes the highlighted one, Clear all is the last row, and Escape closes the panel, then clears the text, then leaves the field. The count is announced when the panel opens and as typing changes it, and removals are announced too. emptyText is the quiet line for a field with no history, label names the field, value, defaultValue and onValueChange control the text, placement keeps the panel under (or over) the field instead of letting it flip when there is no room, and defaultOpen starts with the panel open. rememberSearch, forgetSearch, matchRecent and foldSearch are exported from recent-searches-field/recents for your own storage code.

items.name: autosuggest-field
items.title: Autosuggest field
items.description: A free-text field with suggestions: type a job title or a city and pick a match, or keep exactly what you typed.
items.docs: The value is whatever is in the field: onValueChange receives every keystroke and the suggestion a click or Enter fills in, and value, defaultValue and onValueChange control it. options are texts or { value, hint } with a quiet word beside the text (a country beside a city). They are ranked by what begins with the typed text, then a word that begins with it (designer finds Product Designer), then what only contains it, ignoring capitals and accents, with the match in bold (a single suggestion that is exactly what was typed is not offered again, but one that only differs in capitals or accents is: zurich offers Zürich), and the first maxOptions (6) are shown; with an empty field ArrowDown lists the first ones as they are. ArrowDown opens the list and ArrowDown, ArrowUp move a highlight that aria-activedescendant names while the focus stays in the input. Enter takes the highlighted suggestion; with none highlighted it leaves the text and the form around the field submits as usual. Escape closes the list and keeps the text. onQueryChange(query) fires as the text is typed, so a server can answer with new options; add loading for a spinner and a quiet line while there is nothing to list yet, filter={false} when your source has already narrowed the list, and emptyHint for a line that says nothing matched (without it the panel stays shut). The number of suggestions is announced politely. placement keeps the list under or over the field instead of letting it flip, defaultOpen starts with it open. Other input props such as name, id and placeholder go to the input. rankSuggestions is exported from autosuggest-field/suggestions.

items.name: markdown-field
items.title: Markdown field
items.description: A writing box with a small toolbar and a live preview: bold, italic, link, lists, quote and code, with shortcuts and no editor library.
items.docs: value, defaultValue and onValueChange speak plain Markdown text. toolbar lists the buttons to show (bold, italic, link, bulleted-list, numbered-list, quote, code; all by default) and the shortcuts Ctrl or Cmd with B, I and K follow it. A button wraps or prefixes the selection and takes the syntax off again when it is already there; with nothing selected, bold and italic work on the word at the caret, and the link button writes [link text](https://) with the part to fill in selected. The list and quote buttons act on every line the selection touches (a bulleted line becomes numbered when you press the numbered button), and Enter inside a list starts the next item, or ends the list on an empty one. The edits go through the browser's own editing (insertText), so Undo undoes a button; where that is not available the text is set directly and the selection restored. rows, maxLength (with a counter) and every other textarea prop such as id, name and aria-label go to the textarea, and defaultTab="preview" opens on the preview. The text stays mounted behind the preview, so a form still posts it. The preview is the exported Markdown component (markdown-field/markdown): it renders headings (a # becomes h2, so a page keeps its own h1; headingLevel changes that), bold and italic, links (http, https, mailto, tel, paths and anchors only), bulleted and numbered lists, quotes, inline code and fenced code as React elements, keeps single line breaks and never produces raw HTML. A link to a script or a data address is not made a link: it stays on the page as the plain text that was written. Lists are one level deep, so an indented item is shown flat. Use it wherever the saved text is shown again. applyAction and continueList are exported from markdown-field/edit for buttons of your own.

items.name: image-picker
items.title: Image picker
items.description: Choose one image from a set of thumbnails, such as a cover, a header or a theme, as a radio group with a ring and a check on the pick; or several, up to a limit.
items.docs: images are { id, src, alt, label }. value and onValueChange speak the id (null when the choice is cleared), so what is stored never depends on an address. allowNone adds a first tile that clears the choice. With multiple, value is an array of ids and max stops the choice: the other tiles dim, the count under the grid says so, and a polite message explains it when someone tries; allowNone does not apply. columns (2 to 6) is the number of tiles in a row once the container has room: it follows container queries, so a narrow sidebar gets fewer whatever the screen, and aspect is width over height (16 / 10 by default, 1 for squares). It is a radio group (a group of checkboxes with multiple) with one tab stop: Tab goes to the chosen tile, the arrow keys move through the grid in two directions (Up and Down by a whole row as laid out right now), Home and End jump, Space or Enter chooses. A tile is named by its label, or by its alt text when it has no label, with Selected added when it is chosen, and the alt text describes it when there is a label. A picture that is loading shows the Skeleton, and one that fails falls back to a quiet block with its label. loading draws shaded tiles in place of the pictures, name posts the chosen id (one hidden input per id with multiple), noneLabel renames the first tile, and disabled turns it all off.

items.name: postal-code-field
items.title: Postal code field
items.description: A postcode field that knows the country: it writes 1234 AB, SW1A 1AA or 90210 the way that country does, and says what a valid code looks like when yours is not.
items.docs: country is the ISO code (NL, GB, US) and the field takes that country's pattern, placeholder, keyboard (digits for 90210, letters and capitals for 1234 AB) and spacing from a table of thirty countries. Nothing is forced while typing, so the caret never jumps: when the field is left, the code is written the way its country writes it (1017cj becomes 1017 CJ, 902101234 becomes 90210-1234), and from then on a wrong code is explained live, with what a valid one looks like (Dutch postcodes look like 1234 AB.), until it is right; a right one gets a quiet check. value, defaultValue and onValueChange(code, { valid }) work with the code as the country writes it once it is valid, and with the text as typed (trimmed) until then, so a draft kept in state, or posted through name, is never a string nobody typed. Changing country checks the code that is there against the new country at once (a code that is also right there is rewritten in its style) and reports the new answer. required adds aria-required and, once the field has been left empty, says what to enter (Enter a Dutch postcode, like 1234 AB.); like the other fields it never blocks a submit. A country without a rule accepts any text and shows no message. name adds a hidden input with the code the field reports, and the field carries autocomplete postal-code. countries adds or replaces rules ({ adjective, term, example, alternative, pattern, format, numeric }), and POSTAL_CODES, formatPostalCode, isPostalCode, describePostalCode and askForPostalCode are exported from postal-code-field/postcodes, so an address form or a server can share the table. A code is judged by its shape only: it can be well formed and still belong to no street.

items.name: multi-currency-field
items.title: Multi-currency field
items.description: An amount and its currency in one field: search the menu, and the decimals follow the currency, reported as whole minor units so a yen is never in hundredths.
items.docs: value and onValueChange speak { minor, currency }: minor is a whole number in the minor units of the currency (1250 is 12.50 EUR and 1,250 JPY), or null while the field is empty, and the second argument says whether there is an amount that is allowed. The decimals of every currency are asked of Intl (JPY none, EUR two, KWD three), the amount is written the locale's way when the field is left, and either decimal sign is understood when typing (12,5, 12.5, 1.250,00 and 1,250.00). Changing the currency keeps the typed number, works out the minor value again (12.50 EUR is 13 JPY) and announces the result, rounding included; if the number no longer fits min and max in the new currency, that is said at once and not only when the field is left. min and max are minor units, a number for every currency or an object with one per code, and a refusal names the limit in the chosen currency. allowNegative accepts a minus and asks a phone for the full keyboard, because a number pad has none. currencies lists the ISO codes of the menu (one code shows no menu), labels renames every message and screen reader phrase, and name adds a hidden input with the minor units plus <name>-currency with the code. Pass id for a label's htmlFor; it lands on the amount. With no id, aria-label or aria-labelledby the amount is named Amount, so it is never unnamed.

items.name: percentage-field
items.title: Percentage field
items.description: A percentage you can type or nudge: it understands 12,5 and 12.5%, stays in range, and can show what the rate comes to on a base amount.
items.docs: value and onValueChange speak a plain number (12.5), or null while the field is empty, always inside min and max (0 and 100 unless you say otherwise) and rounded to precision (2 unless you say otherwise). It reads 12,5, 12.5 and 12.5% alike, so the percent sign is the field's own and a typed one is dropped. The arrow keys add or take away step, Shift or Page Up and Page Down make it ten times as much, and Ctrl or Cmd with Home and End go to the limits (Home and End themselves move the caret, as in any field). With a min below zero the field asks a phone for the full keyboard, because a number pad has no minus. A number that was out of range is brought in when the field is left, and a quiet line says so (Capped at 100%.). With base (minor units, 48000 is 480.00) and currency it writes the sentence under the field as the number changes, in the currency's own decimals, and a screen reader hears it once the number is settled; labels renames every phrase. The input is a spinbutton with the value, the limits and the sentence as its text. name adds a hidden input with the number, and id lands on the input, so a label's htmlFor focuses it (with no id, aria-label or aria-labelledby the field is named Percentage).

items.name: amount-presets
items.title: Amount presets
items.description: Pick a gift, donation or top-up amount from preset chips that work as a radio group, or choose Other and type your own within limits.
items.docs: presets is a list of { amount, impact }: amount in minor units (2500 is 25.00 EUR and 2,500 JPY), impact an optional line shown under the chips while that preset is chosen, and suggested names the amount to mark with the words Most popular. value and onValueChange speak one amount in minor units, or null while nothing is chosen and while the Other field is empty or refused; a custom amount outside min and max is never reported, so a form cannot submit it. The chips are a Radix radio group: arrow keys move and choose, the group is one tab stop, and the chosen chip is filled with a check. Choosing Other by click or Space opens the amount field and moves the focus into it (an arrow key leaves the focus on the chip), choosing a preset clears and closes it, and a value that arrives from outside opens or closes it to match. The Other field is written in the currency's own decimals, accepts either decimal sign, and a refusal names both limits in words (Choose between 5 EUR and 500 EUR.) in a polite live region. label names the group, labels renames every phrase, name adds a hidden input with the amount, and currency and locale decide how the amounts are written.

items.name: time-range-field
items.title: Time range field
items.description: A start and an end time with the length between them: type or pick each end, move the start and the end follows, and a bad range is refused in words.
items.docs: value and onValueChange speak { start, end, minutes }: start and end are 24-hour "HH:MM" strings and minutes is the length, with the night counted when the end is on the next day. It is reported once both times are set and the range is allowed, and null whenever it is not, so a form never sees half a range. Each end is an input that takes what people type (9, 930, 0930, 9:30, 9h30, 2:30 pm) and a button that opens the same list of slots the Time picker offers, every step minutes from min to max; the end list says how long each choice makes the range, and slots at or before the start are disabled unless allowOvernight is on, when they show the length and +1 day. A range that ends on the next day says +1 day after its length beside the field too. The arrow keys move a time to the next slot on the grid, Alt+ArrowDown opens the list. Times are settled when the field is left, on Enter, on a pick and on an arrow key, never on every keystroke. An end that is not after the start is refused with the reason in words and aria-invalid on the end input; a time outside min and max, or a text that is no time, is explained on its own input. keepDuration moves the end along when the start changes and says so in a polite live region; without allowOvernight the end stops at max. name adds <name>-start and <name>-end hidden inputs, id lands on the start input (the end gets it with -end after it), and name the group with aria-labelledby or aria-label. labels renames every phrase.

items.name: due-date-field
items.title: Due date field
items.description: A date field for tasks and deadlines: Today, Tomorrow and Next week as chips, a calendar for everything else, and No date, each said in words.
items.docs: value and onValueChange speak an ISO date ("2026-10-23") or null for no date. now (a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string) and timeZone say what today is: Today, Tomorrow and Next week (the coming Monday, a week away when today is a Monday) are worked out as calendar dates in that zone, so a task due tomorrow in Amsterdam is tomorrow for the server too. Without now the browser's clock is read once the page has hydrated and the server marks no quick chip, so nothing mismatches; pass now to render everything on the server. The chips are one radio group with a roving tab stop (arrow keys move and choose, Home and End jump, the chosen chip is filled with a check); Pick a date is the last dated option and opens the Calendar in a popover with its own arrow-key grid, an arrow key landing on the chip does not open it, and the focus comes back to the chip when the calendar closes. The line under the chips writes the date with its weekday and distance in the locale (Fri 23 Oct, in 3 days) and marks a date that has passed with Overdue by 2 days and an icon, and that date stays chosen and readable in the calendar; labels renames every word, and chips replaces the quick picks with { id, label, date } where date is an ISO date or a function of today's. allowPast lets the calendar offer past days, allowClear={false} removes the No date chip, weekStartsOn sets the calendar's first day, name adds a hidden input with the ISO date, and aria-labelledby or aria-label names the group.

items.name: recipient-field
items.title: Recipient field
items.description: The To line of a message: type a name or an address, pick a contact, paste a whole list, and keep addresses that fail visible and marked so they can be fixed.
items.docs: value and onValueChange speak a list of { email, name } (the name is optional) and the second argument says whether every address passed the check and which did not. Chips whose address fails stay in the list: nothing is dropped, they are drawn with a warning icon and a dashed edge, the reason is written under the field (Not a valid address, or the reason your validate returns; with several, the first one's), and a click or Enter on the chip puts its text back into the field to be fixed. Typing shows contacts (initials, name, address, the match in bold, people already on the line left out) in a listbox the input drives with aria-activedescendant; Enter takes the highlighted contact or, with none, keeps the typed text, and so do a comma, a semicolon and leaving the field. A typed address that matches a contact gets the contact's name. Pasting a list split by commas, semicolons, tabs or line breaks, also "Name <address>" and quoted names with commas, makes one chip per entry. Chips are reached with Left from the start of the text or Backspace in an empty field, then Left and Right, removed with Backspace or Delete (the focus goes to the next chip), edited with Enter or F2; only the input is a tab stop. A chip shows its address, or the reason it failed, as a tooltip. A duplicate and the limit set by max are said in a polite line and to a screen reader, and a paste that did not fit says how many went in. validate replaces the default check and may return a reason. contacts is the pool for suggestions, label and hideLabel name the line, name adds a hidden input with the addresses that passed, and labels renames every phrase.

items.name: link-field
items.title: Link field
items.description: A link as a CMS stores it: the text, where it goes and whether it opens a new tab, with the address checked, recognised in words and made safe.
items.docs: value and onValueChange speak { text, href, newTab, rel }: text is trimmed, href is the destination as it is stored, empty while the destination is refused or not a link yet, so a refused address is never reported or submitted, newTab is false for a kind of link that cannot open in a new tab, and rel is "noopener noreferrer" for an external link that does, so the page it opens cannot reach back into yours. The second argument says whether the link is usable: a recognised destination of an allowed kind and, with requireText, some text. The destination takes a web address, a path ("/pricing"), an anchor ("#faq"), mailto: and tel: links, and the bare forms of them: northwind.example/pricing gets https:// in front, ines@orbit.example becomes mailto:, +31 20 555 0142 becomes tel:+31205550142. It says in words which kind it recognised (a line under the field and a matching icon in front of it), and refuses what could harm a visitor: javascript:, data:, file: and other schemes, and a path that starts with two slashes, or with a slash and a backslash. allow limits the kinds (external, relative, anchor, email, phone) and a destination of another kind is explained in words. Messages for what is wrong wait until a field is left (and until a press is over, so a submit is not swallowed) and then follow the typing; the line under the destination always has one line of room, so nothing jumps. The checkbox is disabled, with a line saying why, for anchors, emails and phone links. The preview is the link as a button, with a small arrow when it leaves the site in a new tab. label and hideLabel name the group (a fieldset), name adds hidden inputs <name>-text, <name>-href, <name>-new-tab and <name>-rel, disabled disables every control, and labels renames every phrase.
